We're on git branch feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component in this repo (a Salesforce PWA Kit storefront). The developer reports: "the fix we did to get the hover states working to spec affected how it works via keyboard nav and screenreader/voiceover." I need you to find the exact mechanism so we can plan a fix.

Background already known (don't re-derive from scratch, verify and go deeper):
- The component family is `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/` (organism) composing `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/` and `.../zimmProductCardContent/` (molecules).
- `zimmProductCardMedia/index.tsx` has a scroll-snap image carousel: desktop hover-only prev/next arrows, a touch-only slide indicator, and a keyboard-operable scroll container (`role="group"`, `tabIndex={0}`, `onKeyDown` handling ArrowLeft/ArrowRight) that's supposed to work "regardless of pointer capability" per its own docblock (WCAG 2.1.1 reasoning documented inline).
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/zimmProductCardShared.ts` defines `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY = '@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)'`.
- `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s `carousel` part docblock says the arrows' actual reveal-on-hover now lives in the ORGANISM's own recipe (`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/zimmProductCard.css.ts`, its `root` part), scoped to `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)` on the whole card — described there as "point 6" of that file's own docblock.
- Recent commits on this exact branch (find their real short SHAs and full diffs, don't assume the ones below are accurate beyond being a lead): something like "72ee2a9 arrows hover-gating fix" and "983bddf :has(:focus-visible) stuck-open-hover fix" were mentioned in a prior audit context as recent fixes to this exact hover-reveal mechanism — these are very likely the fixes now causing the reported keyboard/screen-reader regression. Find them via `git log --oneline` on this branch (search for "hover" in the log, or check commits in roughly the last 10-15 on this branch) and get their full `git show` diffs.

What to actually investigate and report:
1. Read `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/zimmProductCard.css.ts` in FULL — especially its `root` part and any `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)` selectors, and its own docblock explaining the hover-reveal design (look for a numbered list of "points" — point 6 is referenced elsewhere as covering the arrows reveal).
2. Read `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/index.tsx` and its `.css.ts` in FULL if you haven't already — focus on `canNavigateByKeyboard`, the `role`/`aria-label`/`tabIndex` logic on the scroll container, the `carousel`/`arrowButton` parts' CSS (display:none by default, revealed how?), and whether the arrow `<button>` elements are also gated by `display:none` at the ORGANISM level in a way that could leave them focusable-but-invisible or vice versa.
3. Find and `git show` the full diffs of the recent hover-gating and `:has(:focus-visible)` fix commits on this branch. For each, explain in plain terms exactly what selector/property changed.
4. Check `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.stories.tsx`'s `play` functions (if any) for keyboard-focus assertions (e.g. `userEvent.tab()`, `toHaveFocus()`) touching the hover-reveal — is there existing test coverage that *should* have caught this, and if so does it look like it would still pass despite the regression (i.e. is the test too narrow)? Also check for any `.test.tsx`/`.test.ts` files in this component family.
5. Reason through the actual accessibility mechanics: `:has(:focus-visible)` only matches when a REAL keyboard-focus-visible descendant exists inside the card. If the arrows/other hover-revealed content are set to `display: none` by default and only flipped to `display: flex`/`block` via `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)` on an ANCESTOR, consider: (a) can a screen reader (VoiceOver) still "see"/announce elements that are `display:none` in the accessibility tree at all — normally no, they're removed entirely; so if VoiceOver users can't reach revealed content via swipe/rotor because it's `display:none` until an ancestor gets `:focus-visible`, and VoiceOver's own focus/interaction model doesn't reliably trigger `:focus-visible` the same way a physical Tab key-press does, that's a real candidate root cause — investigate whether this exact mismatch is what's happening; (b) whether keyboard Tab order reaches the arrows/other revealed controls in a broken order, skips them, or effectively traps focus; (c) whether the "stuck open" bug that `:has(:focus-visible)` was meant to fix might have overcorrected by making the reveal LESS accessible via keyboard than before (e.g. requiring focus to remain within a specific descendant that keyboard nav doesn't naturally land on).

Report back: the exact commit SHAs and diffs found, the exact current CSS/DOM mechanism (file + line numbers), and your best-supported theory (or theories, ranked) for the specific keyboard-nav and screen-reader breakage the developer is describing. Do not propose a fix yet — this is investigation only, feeding into a plan. Be thorough and cite exact file:line locations for everything you assert.

50	 * ZimmProductCardMedia (Step 4) and ZimmProductCardContent (Step 5) with no styling of its own
51	 * for either child. This recipe's entire job is the cross-component concerns neither child can
52	 * own by itself:
53	 *
54	 *   1. THE STRETCHED-LINK OVERLAY. ZimmProductCardContent's `nameLink` renders the one real `<a>`

70	 *      `position: static` by default in its own component recipe, so a positioned ancestor is
71	 *      needed for z-index to apply at all. `close` and `carousel` are the two exceptions:

77	 *          Media's is a single class) and silently won the cascade, knocking the remove button out
78	 *          of its pinned top-right corner into normal document flow (Fix 1). See the inline
79	 *          comment at that key below and index.test.tsx's "Fix 1" describe block for the proof.
80	 *        - `carousel` — Fix 3 (found during the manual real-browser check performed after the
81	 *          round-2 Scorer PASS, which explicitly flagged that check as still outstanding, not by
82	 *          any automated pass). The lift rule used to target
83	 *          `'[data-card-slot="carousel"] button'` — the two arrow BUTTONS individually, each given
84	 *          its own `position: relative, zIndex: 1` — identical in shape to the `content button`
85	 *          rule above, and every jsdom test passed. A real click in a real browser still landed on
86	 *          the overlay, not the arrow. Root cause: `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `carousel` part
87	 *          sets `transform: translateY(-50%)` (to vertically centre the arrow row against `slide`),
88	 *          and `transform` unconditionally creates a NEW stacking context on that element,
89	 *          regardless of its `position`/`z-index`. That traps each arrow button's `zIndex: 1`
90	 *          *inside* the carousel wrapper's own stacking context — it only wins ordering battles
91	 *          against the *other* arrow button, never against anything outside `carousel` (like the
92	 *          content overlay), because the whole `carousel` box is itself just an ordinary
93	 *          z-index:auto participant one level up — and, being earlier in DOM order than
94	 *          `[data-card-slot="content"]`, it lost. Moving the lift to the `carousel` WRAPPER itself
95	 *          (already `position: absolute` from Media's own recipe, so only `zIndex: 1` is needed
96	 *          here, same as `close`) fixes this: the wrapper's own stacking context — not one buried
97	 *          inside it — is what gets compared against the overlay, and it wins outright, carrying
98	 *          both arrow buttons above the overlay with it. This is exactly the gap
99	 *          index.test.tsx's own "KNOWN LIMITATION" docblock warns about — jsdom resolves no
100	 *          stacking contexts at all, so this shipped past every automated check and was only
101	 *          found by a real click in a real browser. See index.test.tsx's "Fix 3" describe block.
102	 *   3. THE HOVER-REVEAL SWAP between price and the PLP/Wishlist size-selector (and Home's
103	 *      hidden-by-default price), gated by the same `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` query
104	 *      `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts` already uses for its own arrows/indicator split. Each reveal
105	 *      rule fires on `:hover` OR `:has(:focus-visible)` on this same root (Fix 2 rework below,
106	 *      superseded by Fix H — see point 6) — `:hover` alone would leave every reveal permanently
107	 *      unreachable by keyboard on a hover-capable device, since `display: none` removes the
108	 *      unconditional-state element from the tab order entirely and nothing but a real pointer
109	 *      hover could ever have revealed it.
110	 *   4. NOTIFY-ME'S HOVER GATE (Fix C, found during the SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit against the
111	 *      real Figma Default+Hover Unavailable instances for all three variations, desktop AND
112	 *      mobile). Three behaviours confirmed together, all different from point 3 above:

127	 *        - Notify-me itself is hover-gated the OPPOSITE way round from price/the size-selector:
128	 *          hidden by default and revealed on hover **only inside `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY`**, not

130	 *          hover; every Mobile Unavailable reference (Mobile has no Hover variant at all, so
131	 *          whatever it shows is the only state a touch pointer ever sees) shows it plainly with no

149	 *      `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts`'s own padding step direction), then shown again from

162	 *      variation (Home/PLP/Wishlist) whenever a card has more than one image; there is no
163	 *      `VARIATION_CONFIG` entry for it and this fix does not add one. `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s
164	 *      own `carousel` part used to reveal itself unconditionally inside its own
165	 *      `[HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]` block — a device-CAPABILITY check, not an actual-hover check —
166	 *      which made the arrows visible permanently on any hover-capable device instead of only
167	 *      while genuinely hovering/focusing the card. That sub-block is now removed entirely from
168	 *      `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`; the `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)` pair here is the only
169	 *      reveal path left, the same mechanism point 3 already established for price/the size-selector.
170	 *      Purely additive to the existing `carousel` z-index lift in point 2 above — that lift
171	 *      already handles stacking once the arrows are visible; this handles visibility itself.
172	 *
173	 *      Fix H (live-browser check immediately after the above shipped): clicking an arrow button

381	        },

384	        },

423	          // wrapper's centering.
424	          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.bag}"]`]: { display: 'flex' },
425	        }),
426	      },

import type { SystemStyleObject } from '@chakra-ui/react';
import { CARD_SLOT, HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY, DESKTOP_QUERY } from '../../zimmProductCardShared';

/**
 * Same hover-capable-pointer gate `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts` already establishes for its own
 * arrows/indicator split — now a shared import from `zimmProductCardShared.ts` rather than each
 * file's own module-private copy, so the two can't silently drift. Governs the price <->
 * size-selector swap below, so both composed children's hover treatments engage together off the
 * exact same media feature, on this shared root.
 */

/**
 * A viewport-width gate, unrelated to `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` above — governs the PLP-only bag-icon
 * mobile hide (Fix D, SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit) below. Also a shared import from
 * `zimmProductCardShared.ts`, same reasoning as `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` above: this and
 * `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts`'s own `root` padding step both need the identical `min-width`
 * gate, and a module-private copy in each file was exactly the drift risk this extraction removes.
 */

type ZimmProductCardStyleProps = {
  /** Home only — see VARIATION_CONFIG in index.tsx. Price is hidden at every breakpoint/pointer
   *  type by default and only appears once a hover-capable pointer actually hovers the card. */
  hoverRevealsPrice?: boolean;
  /** PLP + Wishlist — price is visible by default (Content's own natural rendering; no override
   *  needed for that half) and hides only once a hover-capable pointer hovers the card. */
  hoverHidesPrice?: boolean;
  /** PLP + Wishlist — the size-chip picker is hidden at every breakpoint/pointer type by default
   *  and only appears once a hover-capable pointer actually hovers the card, in the same
   *  media-query gate as the price swap above so both engage together. */
  hoverRevealsSizeSelector?: boolean;
  /** Fix C — true whenever ZimmProductCardContent actually mounted a notify-me button
   *  (`isUnavailable && onNotifyMe`, computed once in index.tsx as `showNotifyMe`). Unlike the two
   *  flags above, the "hidden by default" half lives INSIDE `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY`, not outside it
   *  — see docblock point 4: a touch pointer must see notify-me unconditionally (confirmed via
   *  every Mobile Unavailable Figma reference), where price/the size-selector do the opposite. */
  hoverRevealsNotifyMe?: boolean;
  /** Fix C — true for a PLP/Wishlist card that would normally hover-swap to the size-selector
   *  (`config.hoverRevealsSizeSelector`) but is out of stock. Unlike every other flag here, this
   *  is not a pointer-type concern at all: the size-chip wrapper stays hidden permanently, in
   *  every state, on every device — see docblock point 4. */
  sizeSelectorUnavailable?: boolean;
  /** Fix D — PLP only (`VARIATION_CONFIG.plp.hideBagOnMobile` in index.tsx). A viewport-width
   *  concern, not a pointer-type one: hidden below `breakpoints.md`, visible from it up — see
   *  docblock point 5. */
  hideBagOnMobile?: boolean;
};

/**
 * Recipe for the product-card organism (ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard) — composes
 * ZimmProductCardMedia (Step 4) and ZimmProductCardContent (Step 5) with no styling of its own
 * for either child. This recipe's entire job is the cross-component concerns neither child can
 * own by itself:
 *
 *   1. THE STRETCHED-LINK OVERLAY. ZimmProductCardContent's `nameLink` renders the one real `<a>`
 *      in the whole composed tree. Its `::after` is stretched to `inset: 0` against THIS
 *      component's own `root` — the nearest positioned ancestor. Confirmed by reading
 *      `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts` directly: neither its `root` nor `nameRow`, `nameLink`, or
 *      any other part sets `position` anywhere in that file, so nothing between the `<a>` and
 *      this `root` intercepts the containing-block chain. (`ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `root`
 *      IS `position: relative`, but Media is a *sibling* of Content under this organism's root,
 *      never an ancestor of Content's `<a>`, so it has no bearing on this chain.)
 *   2. LIFTING EVERY OTHER INTERACTIVE CONTROL above that overlay — a z-index higher than the
 *      overlay's own (left unset), or the invisible overlay would intercept their clicks first.
 *      Three separate, single-selector keys rather than one comma-joined selector: verified via
 *      this project's own installed Stylis (v4.2.0 — the same engine Emotion/Chakra invoke at
 *      runtime, confirmed by direct compilation) that a comma-separated list DOES distribute this
 *      recipe's generated class across every branch correctly, but three plain keys need no such
 *      verification to trust at a glance and are each individually addressable from a test. Only
 *      ONE of the three (`content` buttons) also adds `position: relative` — that element is
 *      `position: static` by default in its own component recipe, so a positioned ancestor is
 *      needed for z-index to apply at all. `close` and `carousel` are the two exceptions:
 *      `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own recipe already positions each of them directly (`close` via
 *      `position: absolute, top: 0, right: 0`; `carousel` via `position: absolute, top: 50%, ...`),
 *      so each needs (and gets) only the z-index bump here:
 *        - `close` — a competing `position` value previously declared alongside it had HIGHER
 *          specificity than Media's own rule (this rule is a class+attribute descendant selector;
 *          Media's is a single class) and silently won the cascade, knocking the remove button out
 *          of its pinned top-right corner into normal document flow (Fix 1). See the inline
 *          comment at that key below and index.test.tsx's "Fix 1" describe block for the proof.
 *        - `carousel` — Fix 3 (found during the manual real-browser check performed after the
 *          round-2 Scorer PASS, which explicitly flagged that check as still outstanding, not by
 *          any automated pass). The lift rule used to target
 *          `'[data-card-slot="carousel"] button'` — the two arrow BUTTONS individually, each given
 *          its own `position: relative, zIndex: 1` — identical in shape to the `content button`
 *          rule above, and every jsdom test passed. A real click in a real browser still landed on
 *          the overlay, not the arrow. Root cause: `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `carousel` part
 *          sets `transform: translateY(-50%)` (to vertically centre the arrow row against `slide`),
 *          and `transform` unconditionally creates a NEW stacking context on that element,
 *          regardless of its `position`/`z-index`. That traps each arrow button's `zIndex: 1`
 *          *inside* the carousel wrapper's own stacking context — it only wins ordering battles
 *          against the *other* arrow button, never against anything outside `carousel` (like the
 *          content overlay), because the whole `carousel` box is itself just an ordinary
 *          z-index:auto participant one level up — and, being earlier in DOM order than
 *          `[data-card-slot="content"]`, it lost. Moving the lift to the `carousel` WRAPPER itself
 *          (already `position: absolute` from Media's own recipe, so only `zIndex: 1` is needed
 *          here, same as `close`) fixes this: the wrapper's own stacking context — not one buried
 *          inside it — is what gets compared against the overlay, and it wins outright, carrying
 *          both arrow buttons above the overlay with it. This is exactly the gap
 *          index.test.tsx's own "KNOWN LIMITATION" docblock warns about — jsdom resolves no
 *          stacking contexts at all, so this shipped past every automated check and was only
 *          found by a real click in a real browser. See index.test.tsx's "Fix 3" describe block.
 *   3. THE HOVER-REVEAL SWAP between price and the PLP/Wishlist size-selector (and Home's
 *      hidden-by-default price), gated by the same `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` query
 *      `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts` already uses for its own arrows/indicator split. Each reveal
 *      rule fires on `:hover` OR `:has(:focus-visible)` on this same root (Fix 2 rework below,
 *      superseded by Fix H — see point 6) — `:hover` alone would leave every reveal permanently
 *      unreachable by keyboard on a hover-capable device, since `display: none` removes the
 *      unconditional-state element from the tab order entirely and nothing but a real pointer
 *      hover could ever have revealed it.
 *   4. NOTIFY-ME'S HOVER GATE (Fix C, found during the SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit against the
 *      real Figma Default+Hover Unavailable instances for all three variations, desktop AND
 *      mobile). Three behaviours confirmed together, all different from point 3 above:
 *        - `isUnavailable` suppresses the PLP/Wishlist size-selector swap entirely (index.tsx
 *          AND-s `hoverHidesPrice`/`hoverRevealsSizeSelector` with `!isUnavailable` before they
 *          ever reach this recipe) — there is nothing to pick for an out-of-stock item, so price
 *          stays visible on hover instead of being replaced. Home's own `hoverRevealsPrice` is
 *          untouched by this — its Unavailable Hover reference still reveals price normally.
 *        - Suppressing that swap is not, by itself, enough to reproduce the reference: with no
 *          hide/reveal pair of its own, the size-chip wrapper falls back to Content's natural
 *          (visible) default and would show permanently — briefly shipped exactly that way mid-fix
 *          and caught by re-checking the real render against Figma, which shows size chips hidden
 *          in BOTH states when unavailable, not merely "not swapped in on hover". `sizeSelectorUnavailable`
 *          (index.tsx: `config.hoverRevealsSizeSelector && isUnavailable`) carries that permanent
 *          hide as its own unconditional rule below — deliberately outside `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY`
 *          entirely, since unlike everything else here this isn't a pointer-type distinction at
 *          all: every device sees it hidden, full stop.
 *        - Notify-me itself is hover-gated the OPPOSITE way round from price/the size-selector:
 *          hidden by default and revealed on hover **only inside `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY`**, not
 *          unconditionally. Every Desktop Unavailable+Hover reference shows it appearing only on
 *          hover; every Mobile Unavailable reference (Mobile has no Hover variant at all, so
 *          whatever it shows is the only state a touch pointer ever sees) shows it plainly with no
 *          reveal needed. Putting the "hidden by default" half outside the media query — matching
 *          point 3's own structure literally — would have made notify-me permanently invisible on
 *          touch, since a touch pointer never matches `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` and so could never
 *          trigger the `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)` half either.
 *   5. THE BAG ICON'S PLP-ONLY MOBILE HIDE (Fix D, same SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit). A genuinely
 *      different axis from points 3-4 above: `DESKTOP_QUERY` is a **viewport-width** media query
 *      (`min-width`), not `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY`'s pointer-capability one — a large touch tablet and
 *      a small hover-capable laptop window need to agree with Figma's own Desktop/Mobile split by
 *      width, not by input method. Figma's PLP/PDP Mobile Card-content instance
 *      (`40002163:41479`) has the bag icon's `Icons` frame `hidden="true"`; Desktop's own PLP
 *      instance and Wishlist's Mobile instance (`40002187:58472`) both leave it visible — so this
 *      is `hideBagOnMobile`, one boolean `index.tsx` derives from TWO separate per-variation
 *      config fields (`hideBagOnMobile` proper, PLP's own unconditional rule; and
 *      `hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable`, Fix G's narrower Wishlist-only-when-out-of-stock rule —
 *      see index.tsx's own docblock and `bagHiddenOnMobile` derivation), not a blanket rule. This
 *      recipe only ever sees the one already-combined boolean — it has no opinion on which of the
 *      two reasons produced it. Hidden unconditionally by default (mobile-first, matching
 *      `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts`'s own padding step direction), then shown again from
 *      `DESKTOP_QUERY` up as `display: 'flex'` — not `'block'` — since that is the actual display
 *      type `bagWrapper`'s own recipe uses for its icon-centring; this selector's specificity
 *      (a class + two attribute selectors) beats Content's single class either way, so restoring
 *      the wrong display value would have silently flattened that centring rather than merely
 *      failing to apply — the inverse of point 3's hover-reveal shape, but the same "start from
 *      the narrowest/most restrictive case, widen from there" idea.
 *   6. THE CAROUSEL ARROW REVEAL (behavioural fix, confirmed against the Jira AC — "when on
 *      desktop and the user hovers, then the arrows appear" — and live Figma: the Carousel
 *      element is `hidden="true"` on every Default-state instance checked and visible only on
 *      the matching Hover-state instance, for both PLP and Wishlist). Unlike points 3-4 above,
 *      this reveal is **unconditional** inside `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` — not gated behind a
 *      `ZimmProductCardStyleProps` flag — because the arrows behave identically across every
 *      variation (Home/PLP/Wishlist) whenever a card has more than one image; there is no
 *      `VARIATION_CONFIG` entry for it and this fix does not add one. `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s
 *      own `carousel` part used to reveal itself unconditionally inside its own
 *      `[HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]` block — a device-CAPABILITY check, not an actual-hover check —
 *      which made the arrows visible permanently on any hover-capable device instead of only
 *      while genuinely hovering/focusing the card. That sub-block is now removed entirely from
 *      `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`; the `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)` pair here is the only
 *      reveal path left, the same mechanism point 3 already established for price/the size-selector.
 *      Purely additive to the existing `carousel` z-index lift in point 2 above — that lift
 *      already handles stacking once the arrows are visible; this handles visibility itself.
 *
 *      Fix H (live-browser check immediately after the above shipped): clicking an arrow button
 *      gives it real DOM focus in every evergreen engine, which kept the then-`:focus-within`
 *      reveal true — and the arrows visible — even after the mouse moved back out, until focus
 *      moved elsewhere entirely (confirmed live: arrows stayed up until a click landed outside
 *      the card). The same shared-root `:focus-within` shape underlies every reveal in point 3
 *      too (price, the size-selector, notify-me), so a click on a size chip or the notify-me
 *      button reproduces the identical stuck-open symptom — this fix was therefore applied to
 *      every `:focus-within` occurrence in this recipe, not just this one. `:has(:focus-visible)`
 *      replaces `:focus-within` everywhere in this file: it matches only when the browser's own
 *      heuristic says a keyboard focus ring is warranted, which a mouse-click-focused `<button>`
 *      never satisfies in any evergreen engine, while genuine Tab navigation still does — so
 *      keyboard parity (Fix 2's original reason for adding a focus-based reveal at all) is fully
 *      preserved, and the mouse-click case is not. `:has()` is new to this codebase as of this
 *      fix; it is fully covered by this project's own browserslist (`iOS >= 17`, `Android >= 14`,
 *      `last 4 ChromeAndroid versions`), all far past `:has()`'s 2022/2023 shipping baseline.
 *
 * Parts: only `root` is declared. Everything above is a nested descendant selector inside
 * `root`'s own style object (targeting the composed children's `data-card-slot` attributes), not
 * a separate Chakra part — `index.tsx` never reads anything off `useMultiStyleConfig` but
 * `styles.root`, so `recipeParts.test.ts`'s declared-vs-read reconciliation needs nothing more.
 *

 * .claude/rules/conventions.md's own exception ("0, 1, -1 in obvious idiomatic uses"): it is the
 * standard "one level above the default/auto stacking layer" value, used identically at each of
 * the three lift points, and the stretched-link overlay is deliberately left with no z-index of
 * its own rather than pinned to a specific lower number — so the two sides only ever need to be
 * *some* value vs a *higher* one, never a specific pair.

export const ZimmProductCard = {
  parts: ['root'],

  baseStyle: ({
    hoverHidesPrice,
    hoverRevealsPrice,
    hoverRevealsSizeSelector,
    hoverRevealsNotifyMe,
    sizeSelectorUnavailable,
    hideBagOnMobile,
  }: ZimmProductCardStyleProps): Record<string, SystemStyleObject> => ({
    root: {
      position: 'relative',
      width: '100%',

      // 1. Stretched-link overlay — see docblock point 1. Deliberately no z-index of its own
      // (stays at the default/auto stacking layer), so every control lifted in point 2 below
      // reliably paints above it regardless of DOM order.
      [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] a::after`]: {
        content: '""',
        position: 'absolute',
        inset: 0,
      },

      // type-selector under the relevant data-card-slot root reaches every control uniformly —
      // none of them declare their own data-card-slot, and none needs one: Content's bag button,

      // `close` recipe part already sets `position: 'absolute', top: 0, right: 0` on this exact

      // `.css-root [data-card-slot="close"]` descendant+attribute selector has HIGHER
      // specificity than Media's own single-class rule, so a competing `position` value declared
      // here would win the cascade and knock the button out of its pinned position into normal
      // flow — which is exactly what shipped here before this fix. The element is already
      // positioned (by Media's own recipe), which is all `zIndex` needs to take effect; no
      // `position` re-declaration was ever necessary. See index.test.tsx's "Fix 1" describe
      // blocks for the object-shape and real-DOM/getComputedStyle proof.
      [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.close}"]`]: {
        zIndex: 1,
      },
      // Fix 3 — zIndex only, on the carousel WRAPPER, not on each arrow `button` inside it. See
      // docblock point 2 above for why lifting the buttons individually left them unclickable in
      // a real browser (a `transform`-induced stacking context on this wrapper trapped their own
      // zIndex) despite passing every jsdom test.

        zIndex: 1,
      },
      [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] button`]: {
        position: 'relative',
        zIndex: 1,
      },

      // 3. Hover-reveal swap — see docblock point 3. The unconditional (outside-media-query)
      // half of each flag below is what makes a touch/no-hover pointer see the *default* state
      // permanently: it never matches HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY at all, so whichever rule fired outside
      // it (or the total absence of one) is the only state that pointer type ever sees.
      //
      // `hoverRevealsPrice` (Home) is deliberately NOT here, unlike `hoverRevealsSizeSelector`
      // below it — see Fix E in the [HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY] block: Home's price must stay visible
      // unconditionally on a touch pointer, the opposite of what an unconditional hide here would
      // do.
      ...(hoverRevealsSizeSelector && {
        // PLP/Wishlist: size-selector starts hidden at every breakpoint/pointer type...
        [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}"]`]: { display: 'none' },

      // Fix C — see docblock point 4. Unconditional and permanent, on every device: an
      // out-of-stock item never gets the size-selector, in any state, so this is the only rule
      // for it at all when `sizeSelectorUnavailable` is true (no corresponding reveal exists
      // anywhere, inside or outside the media query below).
      ...(sizeSelectorUnavailable && {
        [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}"]`]: { display: 'none' },
        // Fix F (full-sweep follow-up audit): mobile-only price hide. Figma's Mobile PLP/Wishlist
        // Unavailable references hide price and show notify-me in its place — a genuine swap,
        // unlike Desktop's own additive treatment (price stays, notify-me is simply added on
        // hover, handled by hoverRevealsNotifyMe below). Hidden by default (mobile-first, matching
        // this file's own hideBagOnMobile direction); the DESKTOP_QUERY reveal lives in the single
        // shared [DESKTOP_QUERY] block below, NOT a second one here — see that block's own comment
        // for why a second `[DESKTOP_QUERY]` object key at this level would silently clobber it.
        [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: { display: 'none' },
      }),

      [HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]: {
        ...(hoverRevealsPrice && {
          // Fix E (full-sweep follow-up audit): the "hidden by default" half moved IN HERE from
          // the unconditional block above, where it used to live — Home's Mobile reference
          // (40000223:2821) shows price plainly, and Mobile has no Hover variant at all to ever
          // reveal a price hidden unconditionally like the original shape did. Confirmed live as
          // a real, shipped bug (the Home story showed no price whatsoever at mobile widths), not
          // just a Figma reading. Same shape Fix C already established for notify-me, applied
          // here for the same underlying reason: a touch pointer must never see this half at all.
          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: { display: 'none' },
          // ...and is only revealed here, once a hover-capable pointer actually hovers the card.
          [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: {
            display: 'block',
          },
          // Fix 2 (Scorer rework round 1): `display: none` removes an element from the tab
          // order entirely, so a keyboard-only user on a hover-capable device (tabbing, not
          // hovering) could never reveal this via `:hover` alone. Originally `:focus-within` on
          // this same root — scoped here, not on the price/size-chip wrapper itself, so that
          // focus landing on ANY descendant control (name link, bag button, size chip) triggers
          // the reveal — mirroring zimmSearchInput.css.ts's container/zimmFormRow's own
          // `_focusWithin` sibling to `_hover`.
          // Fix H (live-browser check after the arrow reveal shipped): plain `:focus-within`
          // does not distinguish a real Tab-focused descendant from one that only has focus
          // because the user *clicked* it with a mouse — most browsers give a `<button>` real
          // DOM focus on click, so clicking any interactive control inside the card (an arrow,
          // a size chip, notify-me) left `:focus-within` true, and therefore every reveal below
          // stuck open, until focus moved elsewhere entirely (e.g. a click outside the card) —
          // moving the mouse back out was not enough. `:has(:focus-visible)` fixes this: it only
          // matches when the browser's own focus-visible heuristic says a *keyboard* focus ring
          // is warranted, which excludes a mouse-click-focused `<button>` in every evergreen
          // engine but still matches genuine Tab navigation — so the keyboard case Fix 2 exists
          // for keeps working, and the mouse-click case that produced the stuck-open bug does
          // not. `:has()` is not used anywhere else in this codebase yet; it is fully covered by
          // this project's own browserslist (`iOS >= 17`, `Android >= 14`, `last 4 ChromeAndroid

          // separate string key (not a comma-joined `'&:hover, &:has(:focus-visible) ...'`

          // throughout rather than a Chakra shorthand prop because the descendant-combinator
          // path has to be baked into the selector itself, and Chakra has no `:has()` shorthand.
          [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: {
            display: 'block',
          },
        }),
        ...(hoverHidesPrice && {
          // PLP/Wishlist: price is visible by default (no unconditional rule needed above) and
          // hides only here, in favour of the size-selector reveal alongside it.
          [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: {
            display: 'none',
          },
          // Fix 2 / Fix H — see the hoverRevealsPrice block above for the full rationale.
          // Keyboard focus anywhere in the card must hide price in favour of the size-selector
          // exactly as hover does, so a keyboard user sees the identical revealed state, not a
          // different partial one; `:has(:focus-visible)` keeps that true while no longer
          // sticking open after a mouse click.
          [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: {
            display: 'none',
          },
        }),
        ...(hoverRevealsSizeSelector && {
          // ...and is only revealed here, matching the price swap alongside it.
          [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}"]`]: {
            display: 'block',
          },
          // Fix 2 / Fix H — see the hoverRevealsPrice block above for the full rationale.
          [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}"]`]: {
            display: 'block',
          },
        }),
        // Fix C — see docblock point 4. Both the "hidden by default" declaration AND its reveal
        // live inside this same media-query block (unlike price/the size-selector above, whose
        // "hidden by default" half is unconditional): a touch pointer never matches this query at
        // all, so it never sees the `display: none` below either, leaving notify-me at its natural
        // (visible) default — exactly the unconditional visibility every Mobile Unavailable
        // reference confirms.
        ...(hoverRevealsNotifyMe && {
          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.notifyMe}"]`]: { display: 'none' },
          [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.notifyMe}"]`]: {
            display: 'block',
          },
          // Fix 2 / Fix H — see the hoverRevealsPrice block above for the full rationale.
          [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.notifyMe}"]`]: {
            display: 'block',
          },
        }),

        // 6. Carousel arrow reveal — see docblock point 6. Unconditional (no
        // `ZimmProductCardStyleProps` flag gates it): desktop prev/next arrows behave identically
        // across every variation whenever a card has more than one image. Confirmed against the
        // Jira AC ("when on desktop and the user hovers, then the arrows appear") and live Figma:
        // the Carousel element is `hidden="true"` on every Default-state instance checked, visible
        // only on the matching Hover-state instance, for both PLP and Wishlist.
        // `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s own `[HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]: { display: 'flex' }` used to
        // reveal this permanently on any hover-capable device (a device-capability check, not an
        // actual-hover one) — removed entirely there; this pair is now the only reveal path left,
        // the same `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)` shape as the price/size-selector swap above.
        [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: {
          display: 'flex',
        },
        [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: {
          display: 'flex',
        },
      },

      // 5. PLP-only bag-icon mobile hide — see docblock point 5. A separate, sibling media-query
      // key from HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY above (a viewport-width gate, not a pointer-capability one).
      // Mobile-first: hidden by default, shown again from the shared [DESKTOP_QUERY] block below.
      ...(hideBagOnMobile && {
        [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.bag}"]`]: { display: 'none' },
      }),

      // Fix F+D's shared desktop-reveal block — deliberately ONE `[DESKTOP_QUERY]` object key,
      // not two. A first version of this recipe gave `sizeSelectorUnavailable` and
      // `hideBagOnMobile` each their OWN separate `...(condition && { [DESKTOP_QUERY]: {...} })`
      // spread (mirroring how every other flag in this file gets its own independent spread) —
      // which silently broke, because both spreads produce a property with the exact same
      // *computed key string* (`'@media (min-width: 48em)'`) on the same `root` object. Object
      // spread is a SHALLOW merge: it does not deep-merge two spreads that happen to share a key,
      // it just lets whichever spread comes LAST overwrite the earlier one's value entirely. With
      // `hideBagOnMobile`'s spread positioned after `sizeSelectorUnavailable`'s in this file, its
      // `[DESKTOP_QUERY]` object silently replaced the other's, and the price-reveal-on-desktop
      // rule vanished from the actual emitted CSS — confirmed for real via
      // `document.styleSheets` in a live browser (price stayed `display: none` at 1280px width
      // despite `window.matchMedia('(min-width: 48em)').matches` correctly reporting `true`);
      // every jsdom test still passed, because each one only ever sets ONE of the two colliding
      // flags at a time, never the realistic combination a genuine unavailable PLP card produces.
      // `[HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]` above never had this problem because it was always written as a
      // single key with every contributing condition spread INSIDE it — this block now follows
      // that same shape.
      [DESKTOP_QUERY]: {
        ...(sizeSelectorUnavailable && {
          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: { display: 'block' },
        }),
        ...(hideBagOnMobile && {
          // 'flex', not 'block': ZimmProductCardContent's own `bagWrapper` part sets
          // `display: 'flex'` (it centres the icon inside via alignItems/justifyContent) — this
          // organism's `[data-card-slot="content"] [data-card-slot="bag"]` selector has higher
          // specificity (a class + two attribute selectors vs. Content's own single class) and
          // would win the cascade either way, so restoring the actual display type Content uses
          // matters here, not just "anything visible" — 'block' would silently flatten that
          // wrapper's centering.
          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.bag}"]`]: { display: 'flex' },
        }),
      },
    },
  }),
};

import { breakpoints } from 'app/theme/foundation';

/**
 * Shared DOM-contract constants for the ZimmProductCard organism and its composed molecules
 * (ZimmProductCardMedia, ZimmProductCardContent) — defined once here so every producer (the JSX
 * that stamps a `data-card-slot` attribute) and consumer (the organism's own recipe selectors,
 * plus this component family's test suites) reads the same value instead of each independently
 * retyping it. Same pattern, smaller scale, as `zimmColourSwatchGroupShared.ts`.
 */

/**
 * The ten `data-card-slot` attribute values that wire the organism's hover/reveal CSS
 * (`zimmProductCard.css.ts`) to specific descendant DOM nodes. `media` / `badge` / `close` /
 * `carousel` / `indicator` are stamped by `ZimmProductCardMedia`; `content` / `bag` / `price` /
 * `sizeChips` / `notifyMe` by `ZimmProductCardContent`. Do not rename a value here without
 * checking both molecules' own docblocks, which document what each slot is for.
 */
export const CARD_SLOT = {
  media: 'media',
  badge: 'badge',
  close: 'close',
  carousel: 'carousel',
  indicator: 'indicator',
  content: 'content',
  bag: 'bag',
  price: 'price',
  sizeChips: 'sizeChips',
  notifyMe: 'notifyMe',
} as const;

/**
 * Hover-capable-pointer gate shared by every hover-only affordance across the card family
 * (desktop arrows, the hover-reveal price/size-selector swap, the notify-me reveal) — the
 * resolved SFCC-236 decision that arrows and the touch slide-indicator are mutually exclusive by
 * pointer capability, not viewport width.
 */
export const HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY = '@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)';

/**
 * Desktop viewport-width gate shared by the two places with a real min-width-driven layout
 * change: the organism's own PLP bag-icon mobile hide (`zimmProductCard.css.ts`) and
 * `ZimmProductCardContent`'s responsive outer padding (`zimmProductCardContent.css.ts`).
 * Extracted for the identical reason `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` above was — each file previously
 * derived this independently from the same `breakpoints.md` token, which is exactly the
 * same-value-typed-twice drift risk a shared constant removes.
 */
export const DESKTOP_QUERY = `@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`;

243	  Omit<ZimmProductCardPlpVariation, 'variation'> &
244	    Omit<ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation, 'variation'> &

253	  hoverHidesPrice: boolean;

260	   *  instance has the bag icon's `Icons` frame `hidden="true"`, unlike Desktop and unlike
261	   *  Wishlist's own Mobile instance (bag stays visible there on every breakpoint). A viewport-
262	   *  width concern, not a hover one — see zimmProductCard.css.ts's own responsive rule. */
263	  hideBagOnMobile: boolean;
264	  /** Wishlist only (found during the follow-up full-sweep visual audit against every variant x
265	   *  state node): unlike PLP's unconditional `hideBagOnMobile`, Wishlist's Mobile Card-content
266	   *  instance shows the bag icon when available (`40002187:58470`) and hides it
267	   *  (`Icons` frame `hidden="true"`) only when unavailable (`40002187:58473`) — narrower than
268	   *  `hideBagOnMobile`, and combined with it (not replacing it) in the `bagHiddenOnMobile`
269	   *  derivation below, since the two are mutually exclusive per variation today but there is no
270	   *  reason to assume that stays true forever. */
271	  hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable: boolean;
272	  /** Shown on PLP/Wishlist, suppressed on Home — see the module docblock's "Badge" note. */
273	  showBadge: boolean;
274	  /**
275	   * Allows `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s primary/hover image crossfade for this variation. Suppressed
276	   * on Home per Dani Rivett's scope note, overriding the AC's unconditional framing — see the
277	   * module docblock's "Hover image-swap on Home" note. `false` here means a supplied
278	   * `hoverImage` is simply never swapped to, regardless of pointer capability.
279	   */
280	  showHoverImageSwap: boolean;
281	};
282	
283	/**
284	 * The extensibility AC's actual mechanism: every layout/visibility decision this organism makes
285	 * reads from this table, keyed by `variation` — adding a future variation means adding a union
286	 * member above and one row here, touching no JSX. `index.tsx`'s render body contains no
287	 * `switch`/`if` on `props.variation` anywhere (verify with
288	 * `grep -n 'variation ===\|switch (variation)' index.tsx` — zero hits).
289	 */
290	const VARIATION_CONFIG: Record<ZimmProductCardVariation, ZimmProductCardVariationConfig> = {
291	  home: {
292	    showBag: false,
293	    showAttributes: false,
294	    showSizeChips: false,
295	    hoverHidesPrice: false,
296	    hoverRevealsPrice: true,
297	    hoverRevealsSizeSelector: false,
298	    showRemove: false,
299	    hideBagOnMobile: false,
300	    hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable: false,
301	    showBadge: false,
302	    showHoverImageSwap: false,
303	  },
304	  plp: {
305	    showBag: true,
306	    showAttributes: false,
307	    showSizeChips: true,
308	    hoverHidesPrice: true,
309	    hoverRevealsPrice: false,
310	    hoverRevealsSizeSelector: true,
311	    showRemove: false,
312	    hideBagOnMobile: true,
313	    hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable: false,
314	    showBadge: true,
315	    showHoverImageSwap: true,
316	  },
317	  wishlist: {
318	    showBag: true,
319	    showAttributes: true,
320	    showSizeChips: true,
321	    hoverHidesPrice: true,
322	    hoverRevealsPrice: false,
323	    hoverRevealsSizeSelector: true,
324	    showRemove: true,
325	    hideBagOnMobile: false,
326	    hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable: true,
327	    showBadge: true,
328	    showHoverImageSwap: true,
329	  },
330	};
331	
332	const messages = defineMessages({
333	  // Interpolated with the product name, matching ZimmProductPrice's WAS/NOW pattern — Media's
334	  // own `removeLabel` prop is a plain string, so the interpolation happens here, at the one call
335	  // site that actually knows the product name.
336	  removeFromWishlist: {
337	    id: 'product_card.remove.from_wishlist',
338	    defaultMessage: 'Remove {name} from wishlist',
339	  },
340	});
341	
342	const ZIMM_PRODUCT_CARD_RECIPE = 'ZimmProductCard';
343	
344	/**
345	 * Organism — the full product card, composing `ZimmProductCardMedia` and `ZimmProductCardContent`
346	 * across the `home` / `plp` / `wishlist` variations. See the module docblock above for the
347	 * confirmed Figma variation matrix and this component's own recipe (`zimmProductCard.css.ts`) for
348	 * the stretched-link and hover-reveal mechanics that live entirely in CSS, not in this render
349	 * body — both children are always rendered in full, with every one of their own sub-parts; CSS
350	 * alone decides what is visible for a given variation and pointer capability.
351	 *
352	 * @param props see `ZimmProductCardProps` — a discriminated union on `variation`.
353	 */
354	export const ZimmProductCard = (props: ZimmProductCardProps) => {
355	  const {
356	    id,
357	    href,
358	    name,
359	    headingLevel,
360	    primaryImage,
361	    hoverImage,
362	    images,
363	    currentPrice,
364	    originalPrice,
365	    isPriceLoading,
366	    isUnavailable,
367	    onNotifyMe,
368	    badge,
369	    variation,
370	  } = props;
371	
372	  const { onAddToBag, sizeChipValues, selectedSizeChipValue, onSizeChipSelect, colour, size, onRemove } =
373	    props as ZimmProductCardVariationFields;
374	
375	  const intl = useIntl();
376	  const config = VARIATION_CONFIG[variation];
377	
378	  // Both conditions required — an organism that sets isUnavailable without a real callback
379	  // should not show a dead notify-me button. Mirrors ZimmProductCardContent's own
380	  // showNotifyMeButton co-requirement.
381	  const showNotifyMe = Boolean(isUnavailable) && Boolean(onNotifyMe);
382	
383	  // Fix C (SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit): confirmed against the real Figma Default+Hover
384	  // instances for every variation × Unavailable=True (including the Mobile/no-hover variants,
385	  // which show the only state a touch pointer ever sees) that `isUnavailable` suppresses the
386	  // size-selector hover-swap entirely — there is nothing to pick for an out-of-stock item, so
387	  // price stays visible on hover instead of being replaced. Home's own hover-reveals-price
388	  // behaviour is untouched by this — Home's Unavailable Hover reference (node 40002163:39990)
389	  // still reveals price on hover exactly as the in-stock case does; only the PLP/Wishlist
390	  // hide-and-swap needs suppressing.
391	  //
392	  // Suppressing `hoverRevealsSizeSelector` alone is not enough to reproduce that reference: it
393	  // only stops the organism adding its OWN hide/reveal pair, which leaves the size-chip wrapper
394	  // at Content's own natural (visible) default — briefly shipped that way mid-fix and caught by
395	  // re-checking the real Storybook render against Figma, which confirms size chips stay hidden
396	  // in BOTH states when unavailable, not just "not swapped in on hover". `sizeSelectorUnavailable`
397	  // carries that permanent hide separately, unconditional (not gated by hover-capability at all —
398	  // this isn't a pointer-type concern, unlike everything else in this recipe).
399	  //
400	  // Follow-up (full-sweep visual audit against every variant x state node, not just the sampled
401	  // set the first pass checked): `sizeSelectorUnavailable` ALSO drives a mobile-only price hide
402	  // in the recipe now (Fix F) — confirmed via `get_metadata` that Mobile PLP/Wishlist Unavailable
403	  // hide price and show notify-me in its place (`40002163:41488`, `40002187:58475`), the OPPOSITE
404	  // of Desktop's additive treatment (price stays, notify-me is simply added on hover). Nothing
405	  // extra is computed here for it — the recipe reads the same `sizeSelectorUnavailable` boolean
406	  // for both the size-chip permanent-hide and this new price rule, since both only ever apply to
407	  // the same PLP/Wishlist-and-unavailable case.
408	  const hoverHidesPrice = config.hoverHidesPrice && !isUnavailable;
409	  const hoverRevealsSizeSelector = config.hoverRevealsSizeSelector && !isUnavailable;
410	  const sizeSelectorUnavailable = config.hoverRevealsSizeSelector && Boolean(isUnavailable);
411	
412	  // Fix G (same follow-up audit): Wishlist-only. `hideBagOnMobile` alone only covers PLP's own
413	  // unconditional mobile hide; Wishlist's bag stays visible on mobile UNLESS unavailable
414	  // (`40002187:58470` vs `40002187:58473`). Combined into one boolean here rather than exposing
415	  // both conditions to the recipe — it only needs to know "hide this on mobile for this render",
416	  // not why.
417	  const bagHiddenOnMobile = config.hideBagOnMobile || (config.hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable && Boolean(isUnavailable));
418	
419	  const removeLabel = config.showRemove ? intl.formatMessage(messages.removeFromWishlist, { name }) : undefined;
420	  const resolvedBadge = config.showBadge ? badge : undefined;
421	
422	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_PRODUCT_CARD_RECIPE, {
423	    hoverHidesPrice,
424	    hoverRevealsPrice: config.hoverRevealsPrice,
425	    hoverRevealsSizeSelector,
426	    sizeSelectorUnavailable,
427	    // Same Fix C audit: notify-me is hover-gated on hover-capable devices (hidden by default,
428	    // revealed on hover/focus-visible — every Desktop Unavailable+Hover reference shows it
429	    // appearing only there) but unconditionally visible on touch (every Mobile Unavailable
430	    // reference — the only state a touch pointer ever sees, per the "Mobile has no Hover variant"
431	    // finding — shows it plainly, with no hover to reveal it). This flag is deliberately keyed off
432	    // `showNotifyMe` itself, not `variation`: the confirmed behaviour is identical across all
433	    // three variations, and the recipe's selector simply matches nothing when notify-me isn't
434	    // mounted at all.
435	    hoverRevealsNotifyMe: showNotifyMe,
436	    hideBagOnMobile: bagHiddenOnMobile,
437	  });
438	
439	  return (
440	    <chakra.div __css={styles.root} data-testid="product-card" data-product-id={id}>
441	      <ZimmProductCardMedia
442	        primaryImage={primaryImage}
443	        hoverImage={hoverImage}
444	        images={images}
445	        swapOnHover={config.showHoverImageSwap && Boolean(hoverImage)}
446	        showControls
447	        badge={resolvedBadge}
448	        onRemove={onRemove}
449	        removeLabel={removeLabel}
450	      />
451	      <ZimmProductCardContent
452	        name={name}
453	        headingLevel={headingLevel}
454	        href={href}
455	        currentPrice={currentPrice}
456	        originalPrice={originalPrice}
457	        isPriceLoading={isPriceLoading}
458	        showAttributes={config.showAttributes}
459	        colour={colour}
460	        size={size}
461	        showBag={config.showBag}
462	        isUnavailable={isUnavailable}
463	        onAddToBag={onAddToBag}
464	        showSizeChips={config.showSizeChips}
465	        sizeChipValues={sizeChipValues}
466	        selectedSizeChipValue={selectedSizeChipValue}
467	        onSizeChipSelect={onSizeChipSelect}
468	        showNotifyMe={showNotifyMe}
469	        onNotifyMe={onNotifyMe}
470	      />
471	    </chakra.div>
472	  );
473	};
474	
475	export default ZimmProductCard;

Investigation complete. Here is the full report.

## 1. The commits (exact SHAs, confirmed via `git log`/`git show` on `feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component`)

Three commits are relevant, all found under the "hover" search on this exact branch, in this order (oldest first):

**`72ee2a9` (full: `72ee2a9fc013ba366f39cf59025453dcf8f56af5`)** — Fri Sep 4 23:52:30 2026 +0800
`fix(ui-kits): gate carousel arrows on hover/focus-within, not just device capability (SFCC-236)`

- Before: `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s `carousel` part had its own `[HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]: { display: 'flex' }` sub-block — i.e. the arrows were permanently visible on any device merely *capable* of hover (a device-capability check), not gated on an actual hover/focus interaction.
- After: that sub-block is deleted entirely from the molecule; `carousel` now only ever emits `display: 'none'` (unconditionally, even inside `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY`). The real reveal moves up to the organism's `zimmProductCard.css.ts` `root` part, added as two new selectors inside `[HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]`:
  - `` `&:hover [data-card-slot="carousel"]` `` → `display: 'flex'`
  - `` `&:focus-within [data-card-slot="carousel"]` `` → `display: 'flex'`
- Also updated `index.stories.tsx` (both molecule and organism) to document that isolated Media stories can never show the arrows, and updated both components' test files to assert the new shape instead of the old always-visible one.

**`983bddf` (full: `983bddfe7b79f31585c7e9a540f3e03835835e48`)** — Sat Sep 5 01:27:23 2026 +0800
`fix(ui-kits): replace :focus-within with :has(:focus-visible) in ZimmProductCard hover reveals (SFCC-236)`

- Commit message states the trigger explicitly: live-browser testing of `72ee2a9` found that hovering correctly revealed the arrows, but moving the mouse back out did **not** hide them again — because clicking an arrow button gives it real DOM focus in every evergreen engine, and `:focus-within` doesn't clear on `mouseleave`, so the reveal stuck open until a click landed entirely outside the card.
- Fix: every `&:focus-within` occurrence in `zimmProductCard.css.ts`'s `root` part is replaced with `&:has(:focus-visible)` — for all five reveals in that file (arrows/carousel, price-show for Home, price-hide for PLP/Wishlist, size-selector show, notify-me show), not just the carousel one that was reported.
- Rationale given: `:has(:focus-visible)` only matches when the browser's own heuristic judges a *keyboard* focus ring warranted, which a mouse-click-focused `<button>` never satisfies (in evergreen engines) but genuine Tab navigation still does.
- Also touches `index.test.tsx` (organism): renames every `FOCUS_WITHIN_*` constant to `FOCUS_VISIBLE_*`, and — notably — the commit message says running the *full* test file (not just in isolation) surfaced "a real jsdom+nwsapi quirk: a later plain `.focus()` call stops satisfying `:has(:focus-visible)` once an earlier test in the same file has driven a real `userEvent.click()`-originated focus," fixed by switching that one assertion to `await user.tab()` instead of `.focus()`.

**`8959718` (full: `89597182fb7fd2ba2108dbaeba6e9070edf7da9b`, = current `HEAD`)** — Sat Sep 5 03:18:20 2026 +0800
`fix(ui-kits): use keyboard-originated focus in the outside-card negative test (SFCC-236)`

- Test-only, no behavior/CSS change. Commit message: "CodeRabbit finding on PR #85, verified correct before fixing." The *negative*-guard test ("focus outside the card must not trigger the reveal") used a bare `.focus()` call, which — per the exact same jsdom/nwsapi quirk `983bddf` found — could pass **vacuously** (i.e., report "no match" not because the selector correctly excludes outside-card focus, but because nothing in the whole test file had `:focus-visible` true at that point in the run at all). Fixed by switching to `await user.tab()` plus an intermediate `toHaveFocus()` sanity check.
- This confirms the team was still actively finding subtle focus-state/testing gaps in this exact mechanism as of the current HEAD — three separate rounds of fixes in roughly 3.5 hours, each correcting something the previous round's testing hadn't actually proven.

Repo is clean (`git status --porcelain` empty) and `HEAD` = `8959718`, so everything below reflects the exact code currently on this branch.

## 3. Theories, ranked

**Theory 1 (primary — this is very likely the "screenreader/voiceover" half of the report): `:has(:focus-visible)` is a browser heuristic, not a strict "Tab was pressed" check, and it is not guaranteed to fire for assistive-technology-driven focus.**

`:focus-visible` (and therefore `:has(:focus-visible)`) is explicitly UA-heuristic in the spec — browsers decide whether a given focus event "looks like" a keyboard interaction. A real, well-documented category of mismatch is assistive-technology-originated focus: VoiceOver's own navigation model (VO+Arrow cursor movement, rotor, swipe) moves real DOM focus onto interactive elements without necessarily going through the same code path a literal hardware Tab keydown does, and different WebKit/Chromium versions have handled whether that counts as "keyboard modality" inconsistently. On any Mac laptop with a trackpad, `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` at `zimmProductCardShared.ts:37` is **true** — so this is not a touch-device-only concern; a VoiceOver user on ordinary hardware is exactly the population this gate applies to.

If the browser does not grant `:focus-visible` for that AT-originated focus, `&:has(:focus-visible)` at every one of the five sites in `zimmProductCard.css.ts` (lines 323-325, 338-340, 348-350, 364-366, 382-384) never matches — meaning **all five hover-reveals (arrows, price swap either direction, size-selector, notify-me) stay `display: none` for the entire VoiceOver session**, regardless of how the user tries to navigate. `display: none` unconditionally removes an element from the accessibility tree (uncontested browser/AT behavior, unlike the focus-visible heuristic) — so this isn't "hard to find," it's "not present to find via swipe/rotor at all."

This is a genuine regression introduced specifically by `983bddf`, not a pre-existing condition: the `:focus-within` mechanism it replaced (still described at `zimmProductCard.css.ts:105-109` as the design point 3 reasoning) has no input-modality dependency whatsoever — any focus, however it arrived, satisfied it. Trading it for `:has(:focus-visible)` fixed the "stuck open after a mouse click" bug at the cost of introducing exactly this AT-modality dependency.

Supporting evidence that this exact gap was never checked:
- Zero occurrences of "VoiceOver," "screen reader," or "aria-live" anywhere in `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/` or `.../molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/` (confirmed by grep across both directories).
- `983bddf`'s own commit message cites only "live-browser testing" (which per the story docblock at `index.stories.tsx:335-338` checked specifically "does hover-out hide the arrows again" — a mouse behavior) and jsdom unit tests.
- The test file's own comments are explicit about the boundary of what jsdom can prove, and stop one step short of the AT case: `index.test.tsx` (the "Fix 2" describe block, from line 899, comment block around lines 868-897 and again in the `983bddf` diff around what's now lines 923-936) says verbatim: *"jsdom has no concept of 'focus triggered by a mouse click' vs 'focus triggered by keyboard'... it cannot prove, and only a real browser can, that a mouse-click-focused button is excluded, which is the actual bug this fix (Fix H) addresses."* By the same logic the developer states there, jsdom equally cannot prove or disprove anything about AT-originated focus — that extension was never drawn out or checked.

**Theory 2 (secondary — likely explains the "keyboard nav" half specifically, distinct from Theory 1): the set of Tab stops inside the card is now stateful, which breaks predictable/backward focus order.**

Before `72ee2a9`, the arrows were unconditionally `display: 'flex'` on any hover-capable device (the old `[HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]` sub-block on `carousel` in `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`, removed by that commit) — so they were always a stable, predictable tab stop, independent of any prior interaction. Now, the arrows/size-chip-radio/notify-me only exist as tab stops *while* some element in the card currently satisfies `:hover` or `:has(:focus-visible)` — the number and position of tab stops depends on interaction history, not just DOM structure.

Forward-Tab entry into the card from outside still works, because the first stop (`scrollContainer`, `zimmProductCardMedia/index.tsx:228-236`) is unconditionally present, and landing on it immediately satisfies `:has(:focus-visible)` on the root before the user would reach the arrows anyway. But Shift+Tab entry into the card from *after* it (returning from a later element, e.g. the next card in a grid) lands on whatever the last unconditionally-visible tabbable element is at that moment — traced through the verified DOM order above, that's the **bag button** (`zimmProductCardContent/index.tsx:214-232`), since price is non-interactive and size-chips/arrows/notify-me are all still `display: none`. Only landing there triggers the reveal; the user has already tabbed past the (until that instant nonexistent) arrows/size-chip radio and must reverse direction to reach them. This is a real, mechanically-verified change in behavior — not present before `72ee2a9` — though it's not a hard trap (the controls are recoverable by tabbing the other way), so I rank it below Theory 1 in severity/certainty.

**Theory 3 (lower confidence, worth flagging but almost certainly pre-existing, not introduced by these two commits): the scroll container's own arrow-key handler may not receive raw key events from VoiceOver at all.**

`zimmProductCardMedia/index.tsx:191-195` (wired at line 235) is the documented WCAG 2.1.1 "regardless of pointer capability" safety net (docblock at lines 116-121) — but it depends on the browser delivering a raw `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight` `keydown` to the focused `role="group"` element. VoiceOver typically intercepts bare Left/Right-arrow presses for its own cursor movement on a plain `group` role unless the user has explicitly entered an "interact"/passthrough mode (a non-obvious secondary gesture), so this fallback may not actually reach a VoiceOver user either. I flag this with lower confidence and explicitly separate it from the other two theories because **this mechanism predates both `72ee2a9` and `983bddf` entirely** — it is not something the hover-gating fixes changed, so it doesn't explain a *regression* per se, but it's directly adjacent to the same "regardless of pointer capability" claim and worth the team knowing about while they're in this code.

## 4. Test/story coverage check (would existing tests have caught this?)

No. Confirmed by full read of `index.stories.tsx` (organism, 414 lines) and the relevant slice of the molecule's own stories file: **there are zero `play` functions anywhere in this component family**, and every hover-dependent story says so explicitly in its own docblock (e.g. organism lines 130-136, 330-333/336-338; molecule `MultipleImages` story, per the `72ee2a9` diff) — reason given each time: "Storybook's test runner cannot force a `(hover: hover)` media context." So there is no interaction-test layer at all here, automated or otherwise, that exercises reveal-then-tab-in.

The `.test.tsx` files that do exist (`index.test.tsx` in both the organism and `zimmProductCardMedia`) are narrower than they look:
- The "real recipe assertions" describe block (organism, from line 506, e.g. the carousel-reveal test at line 554) only asserts on the plain-object shape returned by `baseStyle()` — it proves the correct selector *strings* exist, never that a real, revealed element becomes reachable by a subsequent keypress.
- The "Fix 2" describe block (organism, from line 899) is the only one that renders a real DOM tree with the actual recipe class and drives real focus via `userEvent`/`user.tab()` — but it asserts `element.matches(cssSelectorString)` against a hand-built `ANCESTOR_STAND_IN` div substituting for the real card root, not `getComputedStyle().display` (the file's own comments, around lines 871-897, explain why: jsdom doesn't dynamically re-resolve pseudo-class-gated styles via `getComputedStyle` after focus changes). It never queries or tabs onto the real arrow/price/size-chip elements as interactive targets in a fully-composed tree.
- The "every interactive control stays separately clickable" block (organism, line 329, e.g. line 338's carousel-arrow test) queries `getByRole('button', { name: 'Next image' })` and clicks it directly — but this suite's dominant setup mocks `useMultiStyleConfig` to return `{}` for every part (documented in this file's own "KNOWN LIMITATION" preface near the top), so the real recipe's `display: none` is never actually applied to that button in this particular test; the click succeeding proves only that `onClick` wiring works, not that the button is reachable by keyboard when genuinely hidden.

Net effect: this existing suite would very plausibly still pass in full, unchanged, with the exact regression the developer is describing, because nothing in it simulates or reasons about AT-originated vs. Tab-originated focus (jsdom cannot represent that distinction, and the code's own comments say so), asserts real Tab-order reachability into a previously-hidden control after a reveal, or exercises Shift+Tab / backward entry into the card. `8959718` (the newest commit, `HEAD`) is itself evidence of this: even the *negative*-guard test for this exact mechanism had a latent false-negative bug for over an hour after `983bddf` shipped, caught only by an external review tool (CodeRabbit on PR #85), not by the team's own manual or automated verification.
